title: "The Beneficent, the Merciful"
hookLine: mercy, named twice, before the word judgment ever appears

cards: A mare stands in a field with her foal pressed close against her legs. She's about to shift her weight, and she stops, lifts one hoof, and holds it in the air, so she won't step on him.

A saying of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ uses exactly that picture: the gentleness creatures show each other comes from one small share of a much greater mercy. Today's verse is two words long, and both of them are that mercy.

teach.h: THE TWO NAMES FROM VERSE ONE.
teach.b: Verse three: “The Beneficent, the Merciful.” Ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. If that sounds familiar, it should: they're the two names from verse one, the bismillah, said again.
Both come from one root, r-h-m, and the noun is today's word: rahma, mercy.
The same root makes rahim, the womb. In this language, mercy has the shape of the place where you were held before you were born. Why two names?
One common explanation: ar-Rahman is mercy as wide as everything, reaching every creature.
Ar-Rahim is mercy that stays, that keeps coming back to you in particular. And the mare? The same saying says God made mercy in a hundred parts and sent one part into the world.
With that one part, creatures are gentle with each other. The other ninety-nine are kept back. Now look at where the verse sits.
Praise, then mercy, then mercy again, and only after that, tomorrow, the word judgment.
Another saying puts it plainly: when God created the world, He wrote that His mercy outstrips His anger. And in the conversation from day two, God answers this verse too: My servant has extolled Me.

how: Muslims say these two names in every unit of every prayer, twice over: in the bismillah and again in verse three. Ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim are also among the names of God Muslims call on in their own prayers, and children are given the names Abdur-Rahman and Abdur-Rahim, servant of the Merciful.

games.q: what's inside the mercy — tap the pairs.
p: mercy, and the root of womb
the mercy sent into the world

s: the two names in verse three are new to al-Fatiha
they're the same two names from verse one, said a second time.
the Arabic for mercy and for womb share a root
r-h-m: rahma is mercy, rahim is the womb.
in the hadith, God's anger comes before His mercy
the hadith says His mercy outstrips His anger.

games.q: the saying of the Prophet ﷺ says God made mercy in a hundred parts. how many were sent into the world?
games.why: one part, and by it every creature is gentle with another, even a mare lifting her hoof from her foal. ninety-nine are kept back.

practice: Sit comfortably. First, the wide mercy: something good that reaches everyone, sunlight, rain, the air in this breath. Stay with it.
Then the mercy that stays: someone who kept coming back for you, even when you didn't make it easy. Let their face come. If you pray, you can hold the two names: ar-Rahman, ar-Rahim.
If you don't, hold the two pictures.

wordCard.voice: Rahma. Mercy, from the root of the womb, named twice in a row: ar-Rahman, ar-Rahim. Thirteenth word.

orig.note: Arabic: mercy. from r-h-m, the root of rahim, womb, and of the two names ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim.

carryVoice: Your line: mercy twice before anything else. That's the order the prayer keeps. Day thirteen.
